root_cause.fix_direction: give the API a Cloudflare origin (apps/api-cf) and route /api/* to it at REQUEST time from a route handler

first_admin_gap.finding: There is no self-service or ops path to create the FIRST admin account. Every route that could create an admin requires an authenticated admin; the System Owner bootstrap (POST ownership claim) requires the acting row to already be role='admin' AND email-verified AND active; registration creates an unverified 'normal' user and email delivery is the LogMailProvider (nothing sent) on this Worker.
first_admin_gap.consequence: The panel is deployed, gated and reachable, but nobody can log into it until an admin row exists in the staging database.
unblock_options_owner_side: an existing admin whose password the owner holds (the owner reported none)

DB-level provisioning by the owner (Neon staging credentials): insert/update a users row with role='admin', status='active', email_verified_at set, and a password_hash produced by the app's own VeloraHasher so the password policy is not bypassed
a reviewed ops script that does the above with the app's own hasher (not written here — it creates an account, which is an owner decision)
first_admin_gap.not_done_on_purpose: no account, password, token or role was invented; nothing was written to the staging database

resolved.how: owner authorised a database-level provisioning; the password hash was produced by the app's own VeloraHasher (Argon2id, ADR-005 parameters) and the row carries role='admin', status='active', email_verified_at=now()
resolved.tool: a single-use local script (velora-ops/admin-provision/provision.mts) using the owner's Neon key; it refuses to run if any admin already exists, and the deployed credential it replaced was removed — no admin-minting endpoint exists on Cloudflare
resolved.audit_note: no audit_log row was written for the provisioning itself: that table's action vocabulary is CHECK-constrained and actor_user_id is NOT NULL. The first real audit rows are the admin's own actions (USER_STATUS_CHANGED, actor 11)

workers_hashing_bug.symptom: POST /api/v1/auth/register → 500 INTERNAL; login could not have rehashed either
workers_hashing_bug.cause: VeloraHasher uses hash-wasm, which the Workers runtime refuses: 'WebAssembly.compile(): Wasm code generation disallowed by embedder'. needsRehash() sends every successful bcrypt login through hash() too, so BOTH credential paths were broken while every other route looked healthy
workers_hashing_bug.fix: apps/api-cf/src/workersHasher.ts — Argon2id in pure TypeScript (@noble/hashes/argon2.js) producing the identical $argon2id$v=19$m=19456,t=2,p=1$… encoding, bcryptjs for $2a/$2b/$2y, constant-time compare, parameters read from each hash so a future cost bump still verifies old credentials
workers_hashing_bug.proof: apps/api-cf/src/workersHasher.test.ts (6 tests): Worker→Node and Node→Worker verification both directions, identical encoded shape, bcrypt incl. Legacy $2y$, foreign/malformed hashes refused; plus a live register on staging returning 201 and a live admin login returning 200

staging_database.how: the repo's own runner — `DATABASE_URL=<direct Neon URL> npx tsx db/migrate.ts` (NOT a hand-written ALTER); direct (non-pooled) connection because 0042 is DDL
staging_database.idempotency: a second run printed 'up to date' — the runner is forward-only and re-runnable
live_constraint_behaviour: post_edit_body + flow_template_id  -> refused (23514 telegram_post_preferences_flow_stage) — the cross-namespace shape 0042 exists to forbid
staging_database.probe_hygiene: every probe ran inside BEGIN…ROLLBACK; telegram_post_preferences row count is 0 before and after

free_plan_hashing.problem: Workers Free allows 10 ms of CPU per request; Argon2id (m=19456, t=2) needs 200-240 ms, so POST /api/v1/auth/login answered 1102 'Worker exceeded resource limits' on roughly half of all attempts (wrangler tail: 'Exceeded CPU Limit'). WebAssembly — the usual remedy — is refused by the runtime.
free_plan_hashing.solution: the KDF moved into PostgreSQL: apps/api-cf/src/pgCryptoHasher.ts runs crypt($1, gen_salt('bf', 12)) and crypt($1,$2)=$2 inside Neon via pgcrypto (extension 1.3, installed on velora_journal). The Worker spends one round trip, not a KDF.
free_plan_hashing.why_not_weaker: bcrypt cost 12 is a standard credential hash and is the SAME family the Node host verifies (bcryptjs, including Legacy $2y$ imports). No parameter was lowered to fit the plan and no fast/unkeyed hash was introduced.
free_plan_hashing.rehash_policy: AuthDeps gained an optional rehashPolicy; the Worker passes {allowUpgrade:false} because it cannot produce the Argon2id upgrade (rehashing would rewrite the row on every login for no gain). The default is unchanged and pinned by packages/domain/src/passwords.test.ts (4 new tests).
free_plan_hashing.legacy_rows: argon2id rows still verify through the in-worker fallback (workersHasher); the two admin rows were converted to bcrypt so no login takes that slow path
free_plan_hashing.live_check: 8 consecutive logins succeeded before the API's own auth:login limiter (8 per 300 s) answered 429 TOO_MANY_REQUESTS — no 1102 at all; after the window, login 200 → /admin 200 → /admin/overview 200 → session authenticated:true → wrong password 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS → register 201 (DB-side hash) → logout 200
free_plan_hashing.artifacts: apps/api-cf/src/pgCryptoHasher.ts + 6 unit tests; workersHasher.ts + 6 cross-verification tests; 4 domain tests for the policy

session_gate_cold_start.symptom_reported: "نمیشه وارد پنل بشم" — the owner could not get past the login screen
session_gate_cold_start.what_the_logs_showed: auth_events: the owner's browser (Android Chrome) logged in SUCCESSFULLY twice on 2026-10-21 (03:19:59Z, 03:25:37Z, user 13). So the credentials were right and the API accepted them — the failure was AFTER login.
session_gate_cold_start.root_cause: the panel's edge gate (src/proxy.ts) probes GET /api/v1/auth/session with a 1500 ms timeout and fails CLOSED. Measured cold on staging after a 5-minute idle (Neon Free scales to zero): 1.69 s, 1.81 s, 0.98 s. A legitimate session was therefore refused on the cold path and the browser was redirected back to /login immediately after a successful login.
session_gate_cold_start.fix: SESSION_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS 1500 -> 4000, plus one retry before denying (only a transport-level failure is retried; a 200 saying 'not authenticated' is an answer and returns at once). The gate still fails CLOSED — apps/web/src/proxy.headers.test.ts pins that with an unreachable API.
session_gate_cold_start.verified_cold_after_fix: /dashboard 200 in 1.86 s, /admin 200 in 1.38 s, /settings 200 in 2.00 s — all previously above or near the old budget

known_limitations_reported: photo/screenshot AI extraction is REFUSED by design on the Worker: the anonymizer is UnavailableImageAnonymizer (no redaction in workerd), so the ledger records IMAGE_NOT_ANONYMIZED and the user is told to send text. This is a privacy decision, not a fault — but it means screenshot OCR does not work on Cloudflare.
/post shows ⛔ CHANNEL_UNVERIFIED and 23 unfilled fields: the channel is not verified and the daily-bias data is incomplete, so publishing stays blocked by design.
gemini free-tier models are genuinely flaky (503/429); the new retry policy makes short bursts recover, but a sustained 429 still surfaces as «تحلیل با خطا مواجه شد».
